verify-303.summary: Repo guard passed (mvox-app.git). #303 ruling (b, full): blur commits, switch/any-unmount also commits (no silent discard), Escape is the only discard path. At HEAD (post #297, post #302) the rename machinery has NOT yet been changed to implement this — no onblur exists on the rename input, and the collective-switch reset still silently DISCARDS an open rename rather than committing it. Baseline: 281 files / 4340 tests, all green. Two concrete sharp edges found beyond the known double-commit risk: (1) Svelte's DOM-unmount-on-null timing vs blur firing is unverified and needs a live-DOM assertion, not assumption; (2) a more serious, SOURCE-CONFIRMED hazard — routeLoad.ts bumps `generation` BEFORE calling `reset()`, so a naive `reset()` → `submitRename()` wire-up would capture the ALREADY-BUMPED (new collective's) generation inside submitRename's own `const g = routeLoad.generation`, defeating the #297 cross-collective-announcement guard on every switch-commit, not just races. cfg itself stays correct (currentCfg is only reassigned inside the async `load()` step, after reset runs), so the WRITE targets the right collective, but the success/settle bookkeeping does not.

findings.claim: Rename machinery lives entirely in src/routes/roster/+page.svelte (arrange view), state at :2824-2834, guard at :2852, handlers startRename :2854-2860, cancelRename :2862-2868, submitRename :2870-2940, onRenameKeydown :2942-2954, template input :4758-4767.
findings.evidence: let renamingSectionId = $state<string|null>(null); renameValue; renamePending; renameError; renameInputEl; renameStatus (2824-2834). const structuralWritePending = $derived(reorderPending || renamePending || removePending) (2852). submitRename order: `renamePending = true;` THEN `renamingSectionId = null;` THEN `sections = renameSectionNode(...)` THEN `await renameSection(cfg,id,name)` guarded by `if (g !== routeLoad.generation) return;` on both success and refetch-after-failure branches (2894-2922); finally clears renamePending only if generation still matches (2928) but ALWAYS refocuses the trigger unconditionally (2937-2938). Template input at 4758-4767 has `oninput` and `onkeydown` only — no `onblur` attribute anywhere on it.
findings.implication: Commit-on-blur is a net-new handler to add to this one input; no existing blur wiring to adapt.

findings.claim: Current abandon behaviour: focus-loss (no Escape/Enter) does nothing at all — the input just stays open, uncommitted. Collective switch (and any route reload) UNCONDITIONALLY discards the open rename with no write, contradicting the #303 ruling.
findings.evidence: grep for onblur/onfocusout in the file finds only `handleHandleBlur` on the unrelated drag-handle row (line 4807), never on the rename input. The routeLoad reset callback (roster/+page.svelte:155-267) sets `renamingSectionId = null; renameValue = ''; renamePending = false; renameError = null;` (203-206) UNCONDITIONALLY — not gated on `isSwitch` (comment at 189-202 confirms this is deliberate, matching removePending's pattern) — so ANY load (switch or plain reload) silently drops an open, uncommitted rename with zero write. This is exactly the discard path Gama's ruling removes: 'He removed the discard path itself. Starting a rename on another section now commits the outgoing one instead of throwing it away' — that removal has not landed in code yet.
findings.implication: #303 implementation must (a) add an onblur handler on the input that calls submitRename, and (b) change the reset callback so that when renamingSectionId !== null it commits (via submitRename, per Gama's 'reuse the path') before/instead of the unconditional null-out at 203-206.

findings.claim: SHARP EDGE (source-confirmed, more fundamental than blur-timing): routeLoad.ts bumps `generation` BEFORE invoking `reset()`, so any switch-triggered call into submitRename would misattribute the outgoing rename's settle-guard to the NEW collective's generation, silently defeating the #297 cross-collective-announcement fix on every switch-commit.
findings.evidence: src/lib/loading/routeLoad.ts loadForSelected(): `const g = ++generation;` (line 96) runs BEFORE `opts.reset?.({isSwitch, selected: current});` (line 103). submitRename (roster/+page.svelte:2894) captures `const g = routeLoad.generation;` fresh at call time and later gates on `if (g !== routeLoad.generation) return;`. If reset() fires `void submitRename()` for the outgoing collective's open rename, that call reads `routeLoad.generation` AFTER it was already bumped for the incoming collective — so submitRename believes its own write belongs to the CURRENT (new) generation, and its settle-guard never trips as 'superseded'. Result: the outgoing collective's rename-success announcement (`renameStatus = m.roster_section_renamed(...)`) would land in what is now the new collective's live region — precisely the bug class #297's `page.roster-rename-collective-switch.spec.ts` 'CROSS-COLLECTIVE ANNOUNCEMENT' test (line 334) was written to kill, but here guaranteed by construction rather than a race. currentCfg itself is unaffected (only reassigned inside the async `load()` callback at routeLoad.ts:122/+page.svelte:336, which runs after reset), so the renameSection API call still targets the correct (outgoing) collective's cfg/db — only the generation-based settle bookkeeping is wrong.
findings.implication: The switch-commit implementation cannot just call submitRename() from inside reset() unmodified. It needs either: reset() to receive/snapshot the PRE-bump generation (a routeLoad.ts change — call reset before the ++generation, or pass the old generation in), or a commit path that takes an explicit generation parameter rather than reading routeLoad.generation live. This is a design decision the RED-phase spec should force, not something to discover mid-implementation.

findings.claim: The classic double-commit risk (submit's own optimistic unmount firing blur, which re-triggers a commit) is PARTIALLY defended by existing ordering — renamePending is set true BEFORE renamingSectionId is nulled — but only IF the new blur handler routes through submitRename's own structuralWritePending/id===null guards rather than closing over the row's id directly; the actual browser/Svelte-5 timing of unmount-triggers-blur is unverified, not assumed.
findings.evidence: submitRename order (2894-2898): `renamePending = true;` precedes `renamingSectionId = null;` precedes the `await`. Because `structuralWritePending` is $derived and re-read fresh on every guard check, a reentrant call into submitRename() (id read fresh from `renamingSectionId`, or blocked by `structuralWritePending` already true) would self-guard correctly. But if the blur handler is instead written to close over `row.id` / `renameValue` directly (very natural for a per-row onblur) rather than re-deriving from live `renamingSectionId` state, it bypasses that guard entirely and can fire a second, value-identical write — which Gama's amendment explicitly calls out as invisible to a final-state assertion ('Both rewrites are to the same value... A test asserting the final name passes in every case'). Whether removing a focused DOM node synchronously fires blur/focusout in this codebase's Svelte 5 + jsdom/vitest test environment (vs only in real browsers, or not at all in jsdom) was NOT run down live in this sweep.
findings.implication: Spec work for #303 must assert CALL COUNT (renameMock.toHaveBeenCalledTimes) for Enter, blur, and switch as Gama's amendment already states, and should include one test that drives an actual blur/removal sequence in jsdom to settle the timing question empirically rather than by inference.

findings.claim: Spec inventory: page.roster-rename-collective-switch.spec.ts (#297 suite, untouched by #302) has exactly ONE test that will FLIP under ruling (b); the sibling renameError-clear test and the Escape/blank tests in page.roster-arrange-crud.spec.ts stay valid.
findings.evidence: FLIPS: 'CLEARED ON SWITCH (renamingSectionId/renameValue): an OPEN rename input abandoned at switch time does not re-mount on the row after a round-trip through B' (page.roster-rename-collective-switch.spec.ts:452-471) — opens a rename, types 'Half-typed', does NOT submit, switches away and back, and asserts anyRenameInput(container) is null with no residue. Under (b) this scenario must instead assert renameMock was called once with 'Half-typed' (a commit), not a silent clear. STAYS: 'CLEARED ON SWITCH (renameError)' (:427-450) — this is about a rename that already SETTLED with a failure (submitted, rejected, error alert shown) before the switch; unaffected by the abandon-commits ruling since there is no open input left to commit. Also stays: the CROSS-COLLECTIVE ANNOUNCEMENT/STALE DISABLE/CROSS-COLLECTIVE ERROR trio (:333-424, in-flight-write-during-switch scenarios, not abandoned-draft scenarios), the LATE-SETTLE CLOBBER and FOCUS-ON-SUPERSEDED-SETTLE tests (:474-571), and in page.roster-arrange-crud.spec.ts: 'Escape cancels: no write, the row reverts to displaying the ORIGINAL name' (:266) and 'a blank/whitespace-only value writes NOTHING and stays in edit mode' (:303) — both ruling-preserved behaviours, quoted verbatim in Gama's amended spec as 'unchanged'.
findings.implication: RED-phase work: rewrite the one flipping test to assert a commit (call count 1, new name lands, no residual input) instead of a clear; leave the rest as regression pins.

findings.claim: Scope fence: only src/routes/roster/+page.svelte's arrange-view section-rename block is in scope. No other surface shares this machinery — admin's collective-name rename and ProfileField.svelte's generic editable-field pattern are separate, already-independently-implemented code. No locale strings are implicated.
findings.evidence: grep for rename/Rename across src/**/*.svelte returns only roster/+page.svelte (the target), admin/+page.svelte (collective db-name rename, unrelated entity/flow, uses renameCollectiveInStore), +layout.svelte (comments about the admin rename propagating into the collective picker store), +page.svelte (an unrelated showSeasonManageGear-renamed variable, not UI rename), and ProfileField.svelte (comment at :68-71 explicitly naming roster's cancelRename/submitRename and admin's namePencilRef as prior art for 'the house pattern', with its OWN independent editing/preEditValue/activatorRef state — no shared function or state, and it already has its own onblur commit wired at :258/:94). Existing roster_section_rename* strings (messages/en.json:221-224) are reused unchanged.
findings.implication: The #303 fix's blast radius is confined to roster/+page.svelte (+ possibly lib/loading/routeLoad.ts if the generation-bump-before-reset ordering needs to change) and its collective-switch spec file; no i18n work, no cross-file rename-machinery refactor needed.

findings.claim: Baseline suite is green at HEAD before any #303 work.
